subject: Biotechnology
title: Enzyme Replacement Therapy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Enzyme Replacement Therapy usable.

hook.text: Gaucher disease patients lack one enzyme — their cells fill with undigested fat, swelling liver and spleen.

buildup.text: Ceredase was the first enzyme replacement — purified from human placentas. It took 20,000 placentas per patient per year.

discovery.text: Cerezyme replaced it — recombinant glucocerebrosidase from CHO cells, unlimited supply without human tissue.

twist.text: ERT now treats Fabry, Pompe, and MPS disorders — but costs over $200,000 per patient per year.

climax.text: These drugs transformed fatal childhood diseases into manageable conditions — price is the remaining barrier.

punchline.text: Replace what the body cannot make — enzyme therapy is liquid rescue.

quiz.question: Why is enzyme replacement therapy so expensive?
options: The enzymes must be imported from only one country
Production requires complex mammalian cell culture and patient populations are very small
The enzymes degrade immediately and need continuous infusion
